title: add-downgrade-guard-backup-restore-rollback-tooling-private-installer
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: customers running Redwood Private indicated risks during operator upgrades where partially-applied schema migrations or missing backups caused failed rollbacks. This PR adds a set of coordinated safeguards in the private-installer to make upgrades and rollbacks safe and observable: 1) version pinning in Helm + Terraform manifests to prevent unintended auto-upgrades, 2) a pre-upgrade transactional backup-and-verify hook that takes a consistent DB snapshot and verifies checksum, 3) transactional-aware schema migrations (wrapper that runs migrations with automatic rollback on failure), and 4) a downgrade-guard that prevents applying incompatible older versions if schema changes are irreversible. This also includes CLI/workflow improvements to the upgrade/rollback tooling (redwoodctl) to expose dry-run, backup-verify, and force-unlock flows. Checklist: - [x] Pin chart and module versions for critical components (operator, postgres, redis) - [x] Add pre-upgrade backup hook and post-backup verification step - [x] Implement transactional migration wrapper + idempotency checks - [x] Add downgrade guard with explicit unlock flow and explanatory error messages - [x] Add helm/terraform validation and tests - [x] Update installer docs and release notes Risk and scope: changes are focused on orchestration layer (helm values/templates + installer hooks + redwoodctl). No change to public API, but operator behavior during upgrades is altered to be more conservative. Testing: included unit tests for migration wrapper, integration e2e upgrade test that simulates an interrupted migration and validates automatic rollback, and manual smoke testing on a staging cluster. Related: ENG-4521 tracks the migration wrapper work; ENG-4590 covers the redwoodctl UX changes. Jira SUP-1342 was raised during an on-prem customer incident that motivated this work.
commits: feat: add helm version pinning and values for critical charts
feat: add pre-upgrade backup-and-verify hook to installer
feat: transactional migration wrapper with rollback on failure
feat: add downgrade-guard checks and unlock flow in installer
test: add e2e upgrade/rollback scenario simulating interrupted migration
docs: document new upgrade/rollback workflow and redwoodctl flags
review_comments: Marco Li: requested stronger failure messaging from downgrade-guard (added explicit unlock instructions).
Sofia Ruiz: asked for e2e test that simulates network partition during migration — added test that aborts migration worker and verifies rollback.
Kenji Tanaka: flagged potential race when multiple upgrades run concurrently; added a global acquire/release lock in installer and documented it.
Priya Shah (author): replied with implementation details and added telemetry hooks to surface lock contention in Console.
release_notes: Adds downgrade guard and transactional schema migrations; pre-upgrade backup+verify hooks; version pinning for critical charts/modules; upgrade/rollback UX improvements in redwoodctl. No breaking user API changes. Operators should follow documented unlock flow when intentionally downgrading.
deploy_instructions: Deploy via private-installer release: bump private-installer chart to the tagged release, run redwoodctl upgrade --dry-run && redwoodctl upgrade (auto-backup enabled by default). To rollback, ensure backup verification succeeded and run redwoodctl rollback; if downgrade-guard prevents downgrade, follow redwoodctl unlock-downgrade --reason <reason> (requires admin). See docs/installer/upgrade-rollback.md for full steps.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps version pinning conservative for the next two releases to give SRE time to monitor. Telemetry events added: installer.upgrade.started, installer.backup.completed, installer.migration.rolled_back.
